Shell spawn failed (EAGAIN); I'll retry.

I wrote `/app/bin/payroll.py`, ran it on `/app/data`, and saved the result as `/app/out/payroll.json`. `python3 /app/tools/check_payroll.py` prints "OK: every value matches the approved figures." All 150 employees match on every field, and so do the exception counts and totals.

The script uses only the standard library. It reads all nine export formats, including the gzip-compressed files, the repeated headers and the legacy terminals that carry a clock offset. It then applies the rules in `payroll-rules.md` in order, and a run on `/app/data` takes a few seconds.

I wrote the script from the docs rather than from the current files. I only checked it against this period's data, so other periods are untested.

I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | head -100; cat docs/payroll-rules.md docs/exports.md docs/output.md

cd /app; ls data data/exports data/corrections | head -50; cat data/sites.csv data/period.json; head -5 data/employees.csv data/rates.csv; cat tools/check_payroll.py | head -60; head -c 600 tools/reference-digests.json; ls /app/bin /app/out

cd /app/data; for s in exports/*; do echo "=== $s"; ls $s | wc -l; f=$(ls $s/* | head -3 | tail -1); echo $f; head -c 500 $f; echo; done; head -5 corrections/batch-1.csv; file exports/*/* | grep -i gzip | head; sed -n 60,200p ../tools/check_payroll.py
cd /app; tail -5 bin/payroll.py; mkdir -p out; time python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json; python3 tools/check_payroll.py

cd /app; python3 - <<'E'
p='bin/payroll.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("        o_a = zone.utcoffset(datetime.fromtimestamp(a, zone).replace(tzinfo=None)) if False else None\n        cache_off = None\n","")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py | head -1
cat > STATUS.json <<'E'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/payroll.py (stdlib only) implementing the documented formats and rules, and ran it on /app/data to produce /app/out/payroll.json; tools/check_payroll.py reports every value matches the approved figures."}
E
cat STATUS.json
